properties.name: A newcomer can ask their agent what reflow2 is — and is told what it can answer, not what it checks
properties.rationale:
PARTIAL, NOT FULL, AND THE MISSING HALF IS NAMED. `req:explains-itself` is about "someone arriving at reflow2 cold", and that person arrives by one of two doors. A served skill reaches only the one who already has an agent. A stranger landing on the repository sees the README and nothing else, so `cap:explains-itself` (BL-102) keeps that half and stays PLANNED. Claiming full coverage here would have retired a requirement while half its audience was still unserved — the exact overstatement this session spent the afternoon finding elsewhere.

📌 IT CORRECTS A CLAUSE THE REQUIREMENT GOT STALE ON. The requirement says a newcomer must "find where the agent instructions go". Since the user-scope installer there is nowhere to put them: one install per machine registers every project, with no per-project setup, no file to place and no config to write. The skill answers by saying there is nothing to do — which is true, is more useful, and would have been a wrong instruction if written from the requirement's wording instead of from `getting-started/SETUP.md`.

WHY A SKILL NAMED `help` AND A COMMAND NAMED `/what-is-this`. `/help` is a built-in CLI command in the harness and a command file of that name would be shadowed — so the SKILL takes the guessable name an agent reaches for, and the COMMAND takes one that cannot collide.

⚠️ THE LINT CAUGHT A REAL CONFUSION: `adopt` in backticks read as an unknown tool, because `genesis` IS both a tool and a skill and `adopt` is only a skill. Written as prose it would have shipped as a false claim about the tool surface.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
`getting-started/skills/help/SKILL.md`, served and mirrored, reachable by `/what-is-this`. Second of the newcomer pair, after `onboarding`. New capability `cap:a-newcomer-can-ask-the-agent-what-this-is`, satisfying `req:explains-itself` at coverage PARTIAL.

FIVE SECTIONS, and the order is the argument: what it physically is (a program on your machine, a graph as a file in your repo, your agent talking to it over MCP, nothing leaves) — then what it can ANSWER — then the one first move for where they actually are — then what it deliberately will not do — then get out of the way.

⭐ SECTION 2 IS WHY THIS EXISTS AND IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE LEFT OUT. A tool described by its checks reads as a linter, and a person who thinks reflow2 is a linter never asks it the questions it exists for. Four things it can answer that nothing else can: how much of what we said we would build actually works (computed from the thread, not from a status field, so nobody can inflate it by marking their own work done), why it is like this and WHO decided, what breaks if I change this, and where does new work belong. This is the same finding as `fact:the-instruction-surface-routes-to-hygiene-and-not-to-whether-the-thing-works` applied at FIRST CONTACT rather than at orientation.

SECTION 4 IS THE PRICE OF SECTION 2 BEING BELIEVED — four things it will NOT do, said unprompted: it does not read source and build the design for you (`/adopt` has a person in it; two runs need not agree), it does not decide anything for you, it does not judge whether a check is meaningful, and it cannot tell you the design matches reality — only that the files it was pointed at have not changed, and which files nobody pointed it at.
